subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which three nutrients are classed as macronutrients?
questions.explain: Macronutrients (carbohydrate, protein and fat) are needed in relatively large amounts, whereas vitamins and minerals are micronutrients.

questions.q: Proteins are made up of smaller units called what?
questions.explain: Proteins are built from chains of amino acids, some of which are essential and must come from the diet.

questions.q: What makes a protein a high biological value (HBV) protein?
options: It contains all the essential amino acids
It comes only from plant sources
It is high in saturated fat
It provides more energy than fat
questions.explain: HBV proteins, such as meat, fish, eggs and soya, supply all the essential amino acids the body cannot make itself.

questions.q: A vegan wants a meal that provides all the essential amino acids by combining two low biological value (LBV) proteins. Which meal does this?
options: A green salad with olive oil
questions.explain: Combining pulses (beans) with a cereal (bread) is protein complementation, together supplying all the essential amino acids.

questions.q: Fats and oils are made from fatty acids joined to which other substance?
questions.explain: A fat molecule (triglyceride) is made of three fatty acids attached to one molecule of glycerol.

questions.q: Which macronutrient provides the most energy per gram?
questions.explain: Fat provides about 37 kJ (9 kcal) per gram, more than double the energy of carbohydrate or protein.

questions.q: Which group lists only the fat-soluble vitamins?
questions.explain: Vitamins A, D, E and K dissolve in fat and can be stored in the body, unlike the water-soluble B and C vitamins.

questions.q: Which of the following is a monosaccharide (simple sugar)?
questions.explain: Glucose is a single-sugar unit (monosaccharide); lactose is a disaccharide and starch and glycogen are polysaccharides.

questions.q: What is a key function of dietary fibre (NSP) in the diet?
options: It helps prevent constipation and keeps the digestive system healthy
It is the body's main source of energy
It helps the blood to clot
It builds and repairs body cells
questions.explain: Fibre adds bulk to faeces and helps them pass through the gut, preventing constipation and supporting bowel health.

questions.q: What is the chemical name for vitamin C?
questions.explain: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid, needed to make collagen and to help the body absorb iron.

questions.q: Why is vitamin D important in the diet?
options: It helps the body absorb calcium
It helps the blood to carry oxygen
questions.explain: Vitamin D controls the absorption of calcium, which is needed for strong bones and teeth.

questions.q: A lack of iron in the diet is most likely to lead to which condition?
questions.explain: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin in red blood cells, so a deficiency causes iron-deficiency anaemia and tiredness.

questions.q: Why are women advised to take folic acid before and during early pregnancy?
options: To help prevent neural tube defects such as spina bifida in the baby
To increase the mother's energy stores
To reduce the risk of tooth decay
questions.explain: Folic acid (vitamin B9) supports the healthy development of the baby's spine and reduces the risk of neural tube defects.

questions.q: A long-term shortage of calcium and vitamin D in adults increases the risk of which condition?
questions.explain: Too little calcium and vitamin D weakens bones over time, leading to brittle bones (osteoporosis).

questions.q: A 14-year-old girl who has started menstruating should make sure her diet contains plenty of which mineral?
questions.explain: Menstruation causes iron loss, so teenage girls need extra iron to replace it and avoid anaemia.

questions.q: What does BMR stand for?
questions.explain: BMR is the amount of energy the body needs at rest to carry out basic functions such as breathing and heartbeat.

questions.q: An office worker with a very inactive lifestyle wants to avoid gaining weight. What is the best advice?
options: Balance energy intake with the lower amount of energy they use
Eat much larger portions at every meal
Skip breakfast and lunch every day
questions.explain: If energy eaten regularly exceeds energy used, the excess is stored as fat, so intake should match a low activity level.

questions.q: Eating too much saturated fat over a long time is most strongly linked to which health problem?
questions.explain: A diet high in saturated fat can raise blood cholesterol, narrowing arteries and increasing the risk of coronary heart disease.

questions.q: What is the reference intake (RI) for energy of an average adult per day?
questions.explain: Food labels use a reference intake of 2000 kcal (8400 kJ) per day for an average adult.

questions.q: A man has been told he has high blood pressure. Which change to his diet would help most?
options: Reduce the amount of salt he eats
Add more saturated fat to meals
questions.explain: Too much salt (sodium) raises blood pressure, so cutting down helps reduce it; adults should have no more than 6 g of salt a day.
